sq.ANSWER:
• BCD System:
    BCD stands for Binary Coded Decimal. In this system, each decimal digit (0 to 9) is represented separately by its 4-bit binary equivalent. Instead of representing the entire number as a single binary number, each decimal digit is encoded individually.

  • Difference from Pure Binary:
    In pure binary representation, the entire decimal number is converted into one binary number (e.g., decimal 9 is 1001, decimal 10 is 1010, decimal 1947 is 11110011011). BCD keeps each digit independent, so it’s easier to convert back to decimal.

  • BCD Representation of 1947:
    Decimal digits: 1, 9, 4, 7
    BCD:
    1 → 0001
    9 → 1001
    4 → 0100
    7 → 0111
    So, 1947 in BCD = 0001 1001 0100 0111

  • Advantages:

    • Easier to convert to/from human-readable decimal numbers.

    • Useful in digital displays like calculators and clocks.

    • Reduces errors in decimal calculations caused by binary rounding.

  • Disadvantages:

    • Less storage efficient (each digit takes 4 bits even if the value is less).

    • Arithmetic operations are slower and more complex due to the need for corrections.

    • Not suitable for large number computations compared to pure binary.
